extracted.intended_audience: research scientists, journal editors, reviewers, scientific societies, and funders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and operational standards for a scientist-driven, journal-agnostic peer review service that produces an "Evaluated Preprint" to improve manuscripts and facilitate subsequent journal publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of peer review functions (technical vs. impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review should disentangle its dual functions: 1) technical evaluation of data and improving the quality, interpretation, and presentation of a scientific work, and 2) impact evaluation (helping editors assess where the paper stands in the field and suitability for a journal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The service should focus on the first function (constructive technical evaluation) and avoid conflating it with journal 'gatekeeping' or impact judgments (e.g., comments like 'more suitable for specialized journal' or requests for experiments to 'raise its impact').

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientist-driven, journal-agnostic service producing an 'Evaluated Preprint'
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a scientist-driven, journal-agnostic peer review service that produces an 'Evaluated Preprint' — the revised paper linked with reviews and author response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Evaluated Preprint provides authors choices (evidence of productivity/rigor, potential final OA product, or a means to facilitate journal matchmaking) and is intended to add credibility to preprints while remaining independent of journal selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission pathways and author nomination of referees
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit via a preprint server or directly to Peer Feedback and suggest possible referees from the Peer Feedback Review Board or outside referees if disciplines are under-represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing authors to suggest referees helps find appropriate experts while preserving oversight by the service in final reviewer selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial screening for adherence to publishing guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions undergo an initial screening that checks for adherence to relevant publishing guidelines such as plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use screening to remove clearly unsuitable submissions prior to commissioning technical review; screening should check for basic ethical and editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection and minimum reviewer count
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer Feedback will select and contact referees; when two reviewers agree to review, the review proceeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be selected from an extensive Review Board (or outside if necessary); selection aims for impartial, timely, and qualified reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turnaround time: two-week review + one-week consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are given two weeks to complete their reports, followed by an additional week to consult with one another online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 3-week timeline (2 weeks writing + 1 week reviewer consultation) is intended to provide timely, coordinated, constructive feedback; modeled on strategies implemented by journals like eLife and EMBO J.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a review template focused on constructive technical evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: A template for peer review will be created to guide evaluations and emphasize constructive technical assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates standardize reviews, encourage focus on data, interpretation, presentation, and provide consistent structure; direct manuscript annotation is also to be explored as an adjunct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage engagement of junior colleagues in review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are encouraged to engage junior colleagues (e.g., postdocs) in the review process, recognizing strengths each brings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including junior reviewers expands capacity and training opportunities; senior and junior reviewers bring complementary perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer recognition via a credited database
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviewers will receive credit for their contribution in a database that can be used as evidence of public service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public recognition can be used for promotions and CVs; the database should record contributions and be citable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer compensation and credit economy
rubrics_metrics.description: After constructive reviews are obtained, authors (or institutions/funders) pay for Peer Feedback; reviewers may be paid or opt to receive credits usable as authors or transferable/donatable to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a transparent fee structure that recognizes reviewer labor, promotes timely performance, and allows alternatives to direct payment (credits, donation). ASAPbio may subsidize initial costs to increase participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default 'open pipeline' with DOIs and public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The default will be an 'open pipeline' where review reports and the revised manuscript are assigned DOIs and publicly disclosed, regardless of whether the reviewer signs them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open disclosure increases transparency and trust; authors may opt in/out of some visibility features where appropriate but the default aims for openness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response, revision, and possibility of online consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving constructive reviews, authors can respond and revise; the service will explore online author-referee consultation during a defined revision period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide structured opportunities for authors to address comments and for reviewers to clarify points, enabling more effective revisions and potentially faster acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formation of an 'Evaluated Preprint' record
rubrics_metrics.description: The revised paper, the reviews, and the author response will be linked together to form an 'Evaluated Preprint.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This packaged record can serve multiple functions: evidence of rigor for grants/jobs, a standalone OA product in partnership with publication platforms, or a dossier for journal matchmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dashboard for journal editors and journal matchmaking
rubrics_metrics.description: For authors who opt-in, a Dashboard available to journal editors will allow participating journals to view the Evaluated Preprint, submission status, and reviewer identity (if not public); journals may invite submission and indicate acceptance status or request additional work/review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dashboards streamline editor access to vetted submissions, enable invitations for submission, and may lower publication costs if journals accept evaluated manuscripts without redundant review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated reduction of redundant journal review
rubrics_metrics.description: The majority of papers that pass through Peer Feedback are anticipated not to need further review, or only limited review for journal suitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By improving manuscripts and providing reliable evaluations, Peer Feedback aims to reduce cycles of rejection and repeated peer review, saving community time and reviewer effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships with scientific societies for reviewer recruitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will be selected through partnerships with scientific societies, with the Review Board including members who voluntarily agree to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Society partnerships provide credibility, disciplinary coverage, and governance input; societies may offer membership benefits like Review Board membership or discounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review scoring, awards, and performance monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will receive scores on their reviews (from authors, other reviewers, and the community). The system will use these data to create referee awards and monitor performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scores and awards provide incentives and evidence of community service; performance monitoring should identify poor-standing reviewers (low scores and/or slow turnaround) who may be dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance standards and dismissal criteria for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers of poor standing (poor scores and/or excessive time to review) will be dismissed from the Review Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain quality and timeliness by setting clear performance expectations and enforcing them through removal or restriction of privileges for underperforming reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent pricing model and path toward sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a transparent pricing model for peer review services with a path toward financial sustainability, potentially subsidized initially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparent fees help authors and funders understand costs; early subsidies can jump-start participation while sustainable financing is developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility through phased rollout, partnerships, and select reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Build credibility by starting slowly (a few hundred papers initially), fine-tuning the system with community input, and establishing partnerships with prestigious scientific societies and outstanding scientists (junior and senior) willing to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cautious, iterative approach with high-quality participants and society buy-in is essential to establish trust and long-term adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation: focus on validation, not ranking of scientific worth
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer Feedback does not attempt to solve how to rank or evaluate the 'worth' of scientific studies; it focuses on disclosure (preprints) and validation through peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about limits: the service aims to validate technical merit and improve manuscripts, not to replace or determine journal prestige or broader impact metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address potential misuse and community concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate and address questions such as: why use Peer Feedback instead of colleagues; is this an extra layer of review with added time/cost; how to prevent misuse as a proofreading service; whether journals will reduce APCs; recruitment issues given disciplinary loyalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design safeguards (scope-limited reviews, screening, transparency), communicate value propositions (improved first submissions, reduced redundant review), and engage stakeholders to mitigate these concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal of cultural change: peer review for improvement, not gatekeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote a cultural shift where peer review's primary role is improving scientific work and establishing credibility rather than acting chiefly as a gatekeeping mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize training, clear reviewer expectations, and public recognition to shift norms toward constructive, improvement-focused reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and efficiency metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The service aims for a short, defined timeline (approximately 3 weeks) and seeks to reduce overall time and effort to publication by improving manuscript quality and enabling better journal matching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 2-weeks + 1-week consultation model as a benchmark; monitor time-to-review and time-to-evaluated-preprint as key operational KPIs.
